subject: The journey from kitchen survey to fitting
hook: We measure your kitchen walls three times. Here's why.
ig:
We measure your kitchen walls three times. Here's why.

This is how we work at a kitchen survey, and why it takes longer than people expect.

Each wall is measured at floor level, worktop height and near the ceiling, because walls are rarely the same length top to bottom.

Diagonals tell us whether the room is square. A floor level check shows any slope, which affects plinth heights and worktop lines.

We mark sockets, the boiler, the stopcock, waste pipes and radiators, and measure window sill heights, which can limit worktop and splashback heights.

All of it goes onto a survey sketch that travels with your kitchen into our Hanley workshop, so the furniture is built for the room you actually have.

Comment KITCHEN and we'll send you the link to our bespoke kitchens page.
fb:
Ever wondered what we're doing with the tape measure for so long at a kitchen survey?

We measure each wall at three heights, check diagonals to see if the room is square, look at how much the floor slopes, and mark every socket, pipe, radiator and window sill. Walls are rarely straight and floors are rarely level, especially in older Staffordshire houses, so this is what lets us build a kitchen that fits your room rather than a perfect drawing.
